# GA-readiness assessment: inventory TP-to-GA gaps and define the definitive GA scope

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps between current Llama Stack Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. It aggregates TP feedback scattered across support tickets, reviews the current API surface, upgrade behavior, scale behavior, and error handling against enterprise GA expectations, and produces the definitive GA scope that all downstream hardening work is planned against.

## Scope

- Inventory gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar across the four dimensions named by the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Aggregate TP-era feedback from support tickets and other feedback channels into the inventory.
- For each identified gap, record severity and a pass/fail GA-bar criterion.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: which gaps are in scope for GA, deferred, or accepted with documented limitations.
- Obtain product ratification of the GA scope so downstream work is planned against an agreed target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gap inventory explicitly covers all four dimensions (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) — each dimension is assessed and its findings recorded, including a finding of "no gap" where applicable.
- Every identified gap carries a severity rating and a testable GA-bar pass/fail criterion.
- TP feedback from support tickets and other channels is aggregated and reflected in the inventory.
- A definitive GA scope document exists and is ratified by product stakeholders, distinguishing in-scope, deferred, and accepted-limitation items.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, tested upgrade path

## Description

This epic delivers the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack at GA: a versioned API surface, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases. It closes the API-stability gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment and gives enterprise customers the commitment they need to build production applications.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface (OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CRD interfaces as exposed by the distribution).
- Author and publish a deprecation policy defining how API changes are versioned, announced, and retired.
- Close the API-stability and error-handling gaps in the definitive GA scope that fall on the API surface, including scale-limit gaps that manifest as API behavior (timeouts, degradation, and error responses under load).
- Build and run an upgrade test path from the last two TP releases to the GA release, and document the procedure and results.
- Keep existing TP-era API consumers working under the deprecation policy (no hard break at GA).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning scheme is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published covering announcement, support window, and removal rules for API versions.
- An upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA release has been executed and documented as a tested procedure.
- API consumers written against the supported TP releases continue to function at GA, or have a documented migration path per the deprecation policy (rollback/compatibility safeguard for the replaced TP API posture).
- API-stability and error-handling gaps assigned to this surface by the ratified GA scope are closed or explicitly accepted with documented limitations.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.
- Partially serves HLR-1 by executing the API-stability portion of the ratified GA scope.

## Notes

This epic is gated on the GA-readiness assessment: its scope is an estimate until the definitive GA scope is ratified, and the assessment outcome can rewrite the hardening work required here.

# Llama Stack production support posture: SLO targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture for Llama Stack at GA: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a published supported configuration matrix. It converts the TP-era support arrangement into an enterprise-grade, documented commitment.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the supported Llama Stack distributions (availability and operational targets at the level the platform supports for GA components).
- Author the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes, for how long, and how backports are requested and delivered.
- Publish the supported configuration matrix: the distributions, providers, versions, and deployment configurations that are supported at GA, informed by the GA-readiness assessment findings (scale limits, error handling).
- Align the support posture with the platform's existing GA-component support conventions where applicable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented for the supported Llama Stack distributions and ratified by the support/product stakeholders.
- A backport policy is published covering supported release lines, backport criteria, and request handling.
- A supported configuration matrix is published and is consistent with the ratified GA scope and assessment findings.
- The support posture documentation is reviewed and accepted by the owning support organization.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

## Notes

This epic is gated on the GA-readiness assessment: the content of the supported configuration matrix and the SLO targets are informed by assessment findings (scale limits, error handling), and findings may expand the required scope. The policy-authoring approach itself does not change. Scale-limit gaps that the ratified GA scope puts in scope for GA land here only as supported-configuration and documented-limitation entries (this epic documents scale limits, it does not remediate them); remediation of configuration/deployment-level scale limits is planned against the ratified GA scope as follow-up hardening work, not silently absorbed by this epic.

# Promote TrustyAI guardrails integration to a supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

This epic makes the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration a supported integration for GA Llama Stack distributions, replacing the Tech Preview experimental-flag arrangement. TrustyAI is already a GA platform component; this work promotes the guardrails integration between TrustyAI and Llama Stack to the same support level, validated against the stability-guaranteed Llama Stack API surface. The documentation for the integration is authored in the Llama Stack GA documentation uplift; this epic's role for that content is limited to supplying the technical validation input.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental/opt-in flag gating for the TrustyAI guardrails integration in GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Validate the guardrails integration against the versioned, stability-guaranteed Llama Stack API surface and deprecation policy.
- Provide a supported configuration mechanism for enabling and disabling the guardrails integration in GA distributions so the default-on change is revertible.
- Resolve integration defects found during validation that block the supported designation.
- Deliver technical validation input for the integration documentation (integration behavior, configuration surface, support-status findings) to the Llama Stack GA documentation effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The guardrails integration is available in GA Llama Stack distributions without an experimental flag or TP opt-in gate.
- The integration is validated against the versioned Llama Stack API surface, including its behavior under the published deprecation policy.
- Guardrails enablement is revertible via the supported configuration mechanism (rollback safeguard for the replaced TP experimental-flag arrangement).
- Technical validation findings covering enablement, configuration, and support status are delivered to the Llama Stack GA documentation effort.
- No known severity-blocking integration defects remain open at the supported designation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. The documentation aspect of this HLR is authored in the Llama Stack GA documentation uplift, from the technical validation input this epic delivers; this epic owns the supported integration itself.

## Notes

This work is serialized after the Llama Stack API stability guarantee because the supported designation requires validating the integration against the finalized, versioned API surface.

# Enable Llama Stack management by default in the Dashboard for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic makes Llama Stack management available by default in the Dashboard for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. The existing TP-era Dashboard integration for Llama Stack management is kept and promoted to default-on behavior gated on cluster entitlement.

## Scope

- Change Dashboard enablement so Llama Stack management is on by default for entitled clusters, with no TP opt-in gate.
- Preserve the existing feature-flag/default mechanism (OdhDashboardConfig) so enablement can be reverted or overridden per deployment.
- Keep behavior unchanged for clusters without the relevant entitlement.
- Update Dashboard status/caption text that still labels Llama Stack management as Tech Preview where it appears alongside this change (incidental to the enablement change, no new content authored).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is available in the Dashboard with no opt-in configuration required.
- On a cluster without the relevant entitlement, Dashboard behavior is unchanged from before this change.
- The default-on behavior is reversible via the Dashboard's existing configuration mechanism (rollback safeguard for the replaced opt-in behavior).
- No stale Tech Preview opt-in gating or labeling for Llama Stack management remains in the Dashboard.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).
